answer: Grading-correlation anomaly detection resists sybils: cluster identities by how often their grades agree. Honest graders judge independently, so agreement scatters with natural variance like wind in a willow. A collusion ring rubber-stamping its own members shows abnormally high mutual agreement and near-zero variance — a copper sheen too uniform to be real — flagging it for deeper audit. The ring finds no haven in the crowd: its statistical signature diverges exactly where honest disagreement should appear. Precondition: enough overlapping assignments per pair to estimate agreement.
